lessons.title: Google Docs: résumé, assignments and collaborating

steps.title: Shortcuts that save you hours
steps.body: Ctrl+C copy, Ctrl+V paste, Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+B bold. Bonus: Ctrl+Alt+M adds a comment and Ctrl+/ shows all shortcuts. On a Mac use Cmd.

steps.title: A résumé that looks sharp
steps.body: Pick a résumé template in the Template gallery or keep it simple: one font, clear headings via Styles, one page. Download as a PDF (File > Download) before sending it.

steps.title: Working on an assignment together
steps.body: Share the document with your group (Share), set it to 'Editor' and type at the same time. Use Suggesting (instead of Editing, top right) to propose changes without overwriting anything. Via Tools > Explore you can find sources and cite them directly.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Make a one-page résumé with a template and download it as a PDF.

lessons.title: Google Sheets: budget, formulas and filters

steps.title: Your own budget in a sheet
steps.body: Make columns for Date, Description, Category and Amount. With =SUMIF(C:C,"Food",D:D) you add up all spending in one category. That way you immediately see where your money goes.

steps.title: Conditional formatting and filters
steps.body: Choose Format > Conditional formatting to, for example, automatically color amounts over €100 red. Put a filter on your table with Data > Create a filter. Faster lookups: =VLOOKUP and =XLOOKUP.

steps.title: Pivot tables and smart help
steps.body: A pivot table (Insert > Pivot table) summarizes hundreds of rows: drag 'Category' to Rows and 'Amount' to Values. With the Gemini button in Sheets you can ask for a formula or summary in plain language. Always double-check the result yourself.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Make a budget sheet with at least ten expenses, add up per category with SUMIF and color amounts over €50 red.

lessons.title: Google Slides: for school and work

steps.title: Designing without it getting boring
steps.body: Little text, big visuals, at most two fonts. Choose a theme via Slide > Change theme and use Insert > Image > Search the web for royalty-free photos. Don't copy pictures without permission.

steps.title: Transitions: less is more
steps.body: One subtle transition (like 'Fade') is enough. Use animations only to make points appear one by one: Insert > Animation.

steps.title: Collaborating and presenting
steps.body: Share the presentation so your group members can work at the same time. Practice in presenter view (you see notes, the audience doesn't). If you like, ask Gemini for a first draft and adapt it to your own story.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Make a five-slide presentation for a school assignment or internship, with one chart and no slide with more than six lines.
